title: Peach Cobbler with Yoghurt Biscuits
summary: Fresh peaches baked with lemon and topped with quick, tender yoghurt biscuits sprinkled with cinnamon sugar.

ingredients.item: ripe peaches, peeled, stoned and cut in 1.5 cm wedges
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
caster sugar mixed with 0.25 tsp cinnamon, for sprinkling

steps.title: Draw out the juice
steps.text: Toss the peaches with the 50 g sugar and leave 30 minutes, then drain in the colander, keeping 60 ml of the juice. Removing the excess liquid keeps the biscuits from sinking into a soggy filling.

steps.title: Bake the fruit
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Whisk the reserved juice with the cornflour, lemon juice and salt, toss with the peaches in the dish and bake 10 minutes so the fruit is hot when the biscuits go on.

steps.title: Make the biscuits
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate and salt. Stir the melted butter into the yoghurt (it will clump slightly, which is fine), then fold into the dry ingredients until just combined.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Divide the dough into 6 rough mounds over the hot peaches and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 16-18 minutes, until the biscuits are golden and a skewer in the centre of one comes out clean. Cool 15 minutes before serving.

tips: Use whole-milk yoghurt; low-fat versions make drier biscuits.
A common mistake is putting the dough on cold fruit, which leaves the biscuit bottoms raw.
Stir the dough only until no dry flour remains.
Nectarines can be used without peeling.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten warm on the day. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for 2 days; reheat in the oven.
